newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian green group urges greenhouse summit.
newsitem.headline: Australian green group urges greenhouse summit.

text.p: A key green group on Tuesday stepped up the pressure on the Australian government to rein in greenhouse gas pollution, warning of a 65-percent increase in Australia's emission of the gases if nothing was done.
The Australian Conservation Foundation urged the Liberal-National government to call a national greenhouse summit bringing together political, industry, community and conservation groups.
"Australia needs a change in direction on greenhouse," foundation executive director Jim Downey told reporters.
Australia, a major energy producer, is resisting an international drive for worldwide compulsory targets for greenhouse gas reductions.

The European Union is pushing for an international climate change summit in the Japanese city of Kyoto in December to agree a binding target of a 15-percent reduction from 1990 emission levels by the year 2010.

Downey said foundation research showed Australia's output of gases contributing to the greenhouse effect -- thought by many scientists to cause global warming -- jumping by between 20 percent and 65 percent by 2010 unless the government adopted a
"Reducing Australia's greenhouse gas emissions is not only an environmental imperative, it will serve Australia's long-term economic interests," Downey said.

"An important starting point is recognition by the government that the international debate has moved on -- the key issue is not whether Australia should reduce its greenhouse gas emissions, but how best we achieve a reduction."
Canberra says compulsory reductions would hurt Australia's economy and industries more than almost any other country.
But the government has implemented a voluntary programme to encourage companies to reduce emissions of greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane.

"The principal purpose of a summit would be to achieve agreement by industry, government and the community sector about the policies and measures necessary to achieve emission reductions," Downey said.
